 Gold rates in Hyderabad today (Nov 3): Dhanteras and Diwali 2026 gold shopping on mind? Here is 22, 18 and 24 carat price list
 By Upstox News Desk 2 min read | Updated on November 03, 2026, 17:32 IST
 Preferred news source Select Upstox as your Preferred news source SUMMARY
 In Hyderabad, at ₹13,938 for 24 carat, ₹12,776 for 22 carat and ₹10,454 for 18 carat, the city's gold prices are ₹15 per 10 g below Delhi, as of today
 The pearl, ruby and emerald work the city is known for are usually set in 18 carat gold. 
 Gold in Hyderabad was priced at ₹13,938 per gram for 24 carat on Tuesday, November 3, 2026, with 22 carat selling at ₹12,776 and 18 carat at ₹10,454. For 10 grams, the prices are ₹1,39,380, ₹1,27,760 and ₹1,04,535 respectively. 
 Open FREE Demat Account within minutes! Join now 
 With Dhanteras on Friday, November 6, and Diwali on Sunday, November 8, the next four days are the busiest of the year for jewellers in Charminar, Somajiguda and Jubilee Hills.
 Purity Rate per gram Rate per 10 g Change from Nov 2 
 24 carat (999) ₹13,938 ₹1,39,380 +₹510 (+0.37%) 
 22 carat (916) ₹12,776 ₹1,27,760 +₹470 (+0.37%) 
 18 carat (750) ₹10,454 ₹1,04,535 +₹380 (+0.37%) 
 Gold rates in Hyderabad on November 3, 2026; indicative, before making charges and GST 
 The city's rate sits ₹15 per 10 grams below Delhi's, a difference small enough to be erased by a single showroom's pricing. Tuesday brought a gain of ₹510 per 10 grams in 24 carat and ₹470 in 22 carat gold, following a 3.51% fall on October 31. Against October's peak, gold is still roughly ₹12,000 per 10 grams cheaper. 
 Hyderabad's buying pattern is distinctive. Traditional kadas, necklaces and temple sets are almost always 22 carat, while the pearl, ruby and emerald work the city is known for are usually set in 18 carat gold in which the harder alloy holds stones securely.
 Buyers weighing a stone-studded piece against a plain one should note that the two are quoted on different base rates, so a straight per-gram comparison can be misleading.
 Please note that the rates above are indicative. Actual quotes can vary from store to store. So, you should compare rates at more than one jeweller yourself. The amount you finally pay will also be higher than the carat-based price because making charges and 3% are added on top. For instance, 10 grams of 22 carat at 12% making charges can attract GST of ₹4,293, taking the total to about ₹1,47,384.
 Making charges are worth negotiating and comparing as hard as the rate. Every jewellery piece should come with a BIS hallmark and HUID number that matches the bill.
